question.text: The initial velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math> required to project a body vertically upward from the surface of the earth to reach a height of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mi>R</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is the radius of the earth, may be described in terms of escape velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></msub></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi></mfrac></msqrt><mo>×</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></msub></math>.
